title: Decisive Independent Out-of-Sample Evaluation of Terminal Torque and Dynamic Predictors on Plantar Flexion and Resistance Recovery

features: terminal set volume (Norbury Set 4 reps * load)
total volume (Norbury sum of reps * load)
prespecified_hypotheses.utility_threshold: DeltaMAE >= 1.0 Nm (or N) with 95% bootstrap CI strictly excluding zero (p < 0.05)

fixed_model_transfer.source_cohort: Evangelidis et al. (9 men, 27 obs, hamstrings)
fixed_model_transfer.target_cohort: Križaj et al. (21 adults, 42 obs, plantar flexors)
fixed_model_transfer.interpretation: Fixed Evangelidis model exhibits massive out-of-sample degradation on Križaj: MAE increases to 72.70 Nm (bias +72.70 Nm) compared to the local naive retention baseline of 10.48 Nm. Domain shift across muscles and fatigue depth precludes uncalibrated model transfer.

krizaj_evaluation.verdict: REFUTED_INDEPENDENTLY: Adding terminal torque (tau_end) produces a nominal +0.78 Nm gain over MeanRetention (failing the >= 1.0 Nm utility threshold; 95% CI [-0.55, 2.25] spans zero). When compared to the baseline capacity model (PreAlone, MAE = 9.63 Nm), adding tau_end slightly worsens prediction (DeltaMAE = -0.07 Nm, 95% CI [-0.45, 0.32]). Terminal dynamic features offer zero incremental predictive power.

master_conclusion: Decisive independent out-of-sample evaluation refutes the utility of terminal torque (tau_end) and terminal volume for predicting post-exercise residual force. 1. Fixed transfer of the Evangelidis model onto Križaj fails catastrophically (MAE = 47.77-97.63 Nm vs local 9.98 Nm baseline). 2. Retraining on Križaj under LOSO yields a nominal +0.78 Nm gain over MeanRetention (failing >= 1.0 Nm; 95% CI [-0.55, 2.25]),    and actually increases prediction error when compared to baseline PreAlone (-0.07 Nm, 95% CI [-0.45, 0.32]). 3. In Norbury et al., adding terminal set volume increases MAE by +7.25 N at 5 min and +3.31 N at 45 min. Thus, in vivo residual force cannot be predicted from mechanical work or terminal dynamic contraction parameters, confirming that Architecture A's strength-fatigue coupling boundary remains empirically unvalidated.
